A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same flow-model inference-time scaling work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original quantitative and qualitative image-generation experiments, including compositional, quantity-aware, and aesthetic generation, plus scaling experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations, hyperparameter evaluations, and further scaling and runtime results.

M1.justification: SDE conversion, interpolant conversion, and Rollover Budget Forcing retain the same equations and Algorithms 1–2. The adaptive scheduler and default diffusion coefficient are also unchanged; new ablations investigate the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage remains the 121 compositional GenAI-Bench prompts, 100 quantity-aware T2I-CompBench++ prompts, and 45 animal prompts for aesthetic generation. The added compositional scaling study reuses the existing GenAI-Bench prompts.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain BoN, SoP, SMC implemented using DAS, CoDe, and SVDD. The aesthetic DPS comparisons and diffusion-versus-flow model comparison also retain their comparator membership. New component variants serve as ablations.

E3.justification: v5 adds LPIPS-MPD diversity evaluation, isolated timestep/coefficient controls, and tests of 10 versus 20 denoising steps and scaled linear/quadratic diffusion coefficients. It also extends the 50–1000-NFE scaling protocol to compositional generation. Existing main-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 substantially strengthens analysis of the design choices: Table 1 first isolates timestep conversion and diffusion-coefficient scaling, while Table 8 tests step-count and noise-schedule sensitivity. Appendix E.3 additionally examines compositional scaling and computational costs. These add controlled evidence beyond v3's diversity illustrations and quantity-aware scaling analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ±1-sigma NFE-allocation analysis in Figure 9, without adding run counts, seeds, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance. v5's checklist newly explains that computational constraints prevented error bars, but the statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantive numerical findings on component effects, diversity–quality tradeoffs, compositional scaling, and runtime in Tables 1, 5, 7, and 8. Newly reported 1000-NFE compositional VQAScores are 0.9283 for RBF and 0.8886 for BoN. Existing headline scores remain unchanged. The reported 500-NFE compositional runtime changes from 879.10 to 635.01 seconds without an explanation establishing a comparable-setting speedup.

T1.justification: v5 adds an explicit denoising-versus-verification cost analysis in Appendix E.3 and Table 6, and extends the proposal-variance reasoning. The target-distribution, optimal-policy, and SDE proofs remain unchanged. The diffusion-rescaling formula already appeared in v3 Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions, performance-superiority claims, and claimed compatibility with gradient-based guidance. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v5 Section 5 explains how coefficient scaling alone can inject excessive noise and why pairing it with timestep conversion preserves useful diversity. The ablation discussion and Appendix F.1 add interpretations of this tradeoff and the default hyperparameters. The conclusion's overhead and misuse limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 documents the empirical rationale for the already specified 10-step and 3t² settings, expands compositional runtime reporting across budgets, and explicitly states that code is publicly released. The GPU and memory disclosures are retained. The earlier quantity-aware runtime of 809.51 seconds is no longer reported.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 72 research works and retain the same related-work discussion, including positioning against SoP and the claimed novelty of reverse-kernel particle sampling for flow models.

P1.justification: v3 Appendix C is expanded and promoted to v5 Section 5, with corresponding section renumbering. v5 adds acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist, and localized experimental explanations. Most existing narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds tables for ablations, compositional scaling, complexity, runtime, and hyperparameters, plus a compositional scaling plot. The log-SNR figure moves into the main text and the quantity-scaling plot is redrawn. Existing benchmark charts and qualitative grids retain their content and general format.

improvement.justification: The controlled interpolant ablation, hyperparameter tests, and compositional scaling results strengthen support for existing design choices, while the expanded main-text analysis improves explanation. These provide a clear but limited overall gain. Performance uncertainty remains unreported, and the unexplained runtime replacement limits conclusions about computational improvement.
